headline: High-risk write-and-upload pairing: CrewAI can alter local files while social-auto-upload can transmit account-linked media, creating default-path leakage and cascading action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI reads and writes the host working directory and uses stdin/stdout, so manual copy-paste or file-based instruction injection is plausible. social-auto-upload mainly consumes local media/account files and does not expose a shared parser or MCP bridge. The pathway exists, but it is not a default shared channel and the blast radius is limited.
conditions: IF the operator copies untrusted text from CrewAI outputs into social-auto-upload inputs, injection becomes possible.
IF both agents are pointed at the same working directory, file-based prompt injection becomes easier.
mitigations: Keep the agents in separate directories.
Do not paste CrewAI output into upload captions or metadata without review.
Use a human approval step for any text that will be reused across agents.
requires-engineering: add content provenance tags to shared files.

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI has broad network egress and reads/writes the host working directory, while social-auto-upload handles account data and media files. If they share a workspace, CrewAI can expose files that social-auto-upload later uploads, creating a default-path leakage risk. The pair does not show a built-in isolation boundary, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents share the same working directory, files created by CrewAI can be picked up by social-auto-upload.
IF CrewAI is given secrets or sensitive crew data, those files may be transmitted through the upload workflow.
mitigations: Use separate workspaces for each agent.
Store secrets outside any shared directory.
Restrict CrewAI output paths to a non-uploaded folder.
Review upload queues before execution.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem ACLs.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while social-auto-upload does not write files or modify git state. Their write surfaces do not obviously overlap, so direct resource conflict is limited. Because the pairwise orchestration model is developer-defined for CrewAI, uncertainty remains, but the conflict surface is still small.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write into the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF the orchestrator maps both agents to the same account file, account-state races can occur.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Avoid concurrent writes to shared account files.
Serialize any file-producing steps.
Use lock files for shared artifacts.
requires-engineering: add transactional state management.

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate text and artifacts that social-auto-upload may treat as operational inputs, and the upload tool can then act on them without an explicit verification layer in the profile. That creates a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's action trigger. The blast radius is multiple posts or uploads, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF social-auto-upload consumes CrewAI-generated captions, filenames, or manifests without review, erroneous actions can propagate.
IF CrewAI is tasked with producing upload-ready assets, B may execute those outputs directly.
mitigations: Require human review before upload.
Validate filenames and captions against a schema.
Separate generation and execution steps.
Log the source of every uploaded artifact.
requires-engineering: add a verification gate between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and only expose generic docs-level evidence, so there is no documented residency or certification mismatch to cite. However, CrewAI handles API keys and broad crew data while social-auto-upload handles account data and uploads to third-party platforms, so compliance gaps could arise if regulated data is placed into the pair. The other agent is not cited because no specific mismatch is documented.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into CrewAI outputs and then uploaded by social-auto-upload, compliance obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator uses EU PII or PHI in either workflow, a policy review is required.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in both agents.
Review retention settings for uploaded media.
Keep API keys out of shared files.
Document data handling responsibilities.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls.
